correctness.rationale: Re-audited /workspace/repairs/4/RESULT.md and SLOGAN.txt. The generic two-order extension property realizes each of the two-gap placements, and ultrahomogeneity over the named base identifies their complete types. Parity and size limit discrepancy two to the three stated diagonals with exactly 3(n-1) candidates. The repaired proof assigns P_i subset Q_(i+2) to the inverse-displacement inequality and Q_i subset P_(i+2) to the forward inequality (the frozen prose interchanged the order). The diagonal contribution tests one crossing in each direction across every proper prefix cut. Each nontrivial permutation cycle occupies all cuts between its extrema; distinct cycles cannot overlap in a cut, and adjacent cut intervals would share a vertex, so all cuts belong to one cycle joining 1 to n. For n>=4 the endpoints' displacement excludes its being a transposition. A fixed internal vertex would require that cycle to traverse the unique admissible edge over that vertex both ways, which would make the cycle a transposition. The path-square Hamilton cycle is unique by deleting vertex 1 and contracting 2-1-3 into 2-3, with an inverse at each stage down to the triangle. The explicit zigzag has the two end edges and every length-two edge, hence crosses each proper cut twice and either orientation meets the directed condition. For n=2 and 3, the displacement conditions are vacuous and the diagonal checks give the listed exceptions. Independently enumerated direct pairwise order comparisons for all base permutations of sizes 2 through 7 with exact matching maxima and equality lists (python3 /workspace/reproductions/4.py); not used as the all-size proof. Frozen verification script and recorded output remain applicable.
